blocks.content: The functions of the Commission are mainly recommendatory in nature, possessing no power to punish the violators of human rights or to grant immediate relief to the victim.

items: Limitation Period: NHRC cannot inquire into any matter after the expiry of 1 year from the date on which the human rights violation occurred.
Armed Forces Jurisdiction: In cases of human rights violations by armed forces, NHRC can only seek a report from the Central Government and make recommendations.
Removal Distinction: While members of SHRC are appointed by the Governor, they can only be removed by the President of India, similar to NHRC members.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: NHRC can inquire into human rights violations either suo motu (on its own initiative) or based on petitions submitted by victims.
The Commission possesses the powers of a civil court trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
It has the authority to visit jails and detention centers to study inmate conditions and recommend remedial measures.
NHRC reviews constitutional and legal safeguards for human rights protection and recommends effective implementation strategies.
Its functions are primarily advisory; it lacks the authority to enforce decisions, punish violators, or directly award monetary relief.
